facts.fact: Proclamation No. 590/2008 on Freedom of the Mass Media and Access to Information, dated 4 December 2008, is proclaimed under Article 55(1) of the Constitution; its preamble affirms individuals' right to access information held by public bodies and a legal obligation on public officials to facilitate it (only the preamble is in the captured text).

facts.fact: The media law working group prepared a draft Access to Information Proclamation, consulted stakeholders and submitted it to the Ministry of Justice; the document says it is not yet passed, not under deliberation, and, per a Ministry of Justice expert (interview 2023-03-01), not among the government's legislative priorities.

The document lists the Mass Media and Access to Information Proclamation No. 590/2008 among Ethiopia's laws and says the Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman was designated the organ responsible for implementing freedom of information, and that studies find it ineffective for lack of resources to evaluate public bodies; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

facts.fact: Ethiopia Insider reports that the House of Peoples' Representatives passed the Freedom of Information proclamation unanimously on 25 June 2026, after the draft was referred to its democracy affairs committee on 7 April 2026; no promulgation is reported.

Birr Metrics reports a draft access to information proclamation to replace Proclamation 590/2008, first drafted in 2018, has been forwarded to the Ministry of Justice and has not been presented to the Council of Ministers.
Birr Metrics reports Ethiopia's access to information framework dates from Proclamation No. 590/2008, which the draft is meant to replace.
